name: Feste & Festività
desc: Holidays, from dolcetto o scherzetto to the Befana

vocabulary.ex: La festa di Halloween è venerdì.
vocabulary.exEn: The Halloween party is on Friday.
vocabulary.note: One word covers party AND holiday — context does the work.
Pumpkin-carving is an American import, but it's been fully adopted — like Halloween itself.

vocabulary.exEn: The witch flies on the broom.
There's a ghost in the attic!
vocabulary.note: Masculine despite ending in -a: il fantasma. Italian gender rules love a haunting.
A dolcetto is any little sweet — the Halloween phrase is the only place most Italians meet it.

vocabulary.exEn: You played a prank on me!
vocabulary.note: Also the reply to a compliment you don't take seriously: 'Scherzo!' = just kidding.

vocabulary.ex: I bambini si mascherano da streghe.
vocabulary.exEn: The kids dress up as witches.
vocabulary.note: Reflexive, and 'da' for what you're dressed as: mascherarsi da zombie.
Il Natale with the article in a sentence, but 'Buon Natale' without — greetings drop it.
Babbo, not 'Santa' — Santa is a saint in Italy, and she doesn't do deliveries.

vocabulary.exEn: On Christmas Eve you eat fish.
vocabulary.note: Meat-free fish dinner on the 24th — a tradition enforced with more rigor than most laws.

vocabulary.ex: Preferisci il panettone o il pandoro?
vocabulary.exEn: Do you prefer panettone or pandoro?
vocabulary.note: The December war: candied fruit (panettone) vs plain buttery (pandoro). Choosing a side is mandatory.

vocabulary.ex: A Napoli il presepe è un'arte.
vocabulary.exEn: In Naples the nativity scene is an art form.
vocabulary.note: Neapolitan presepi include artisan figurines of literally everyone — politicians included.

vocabulary.en: New Year's Eve / New Year's Day
vocabulary.note: Capo-danno: 'head of the year'. Covers both the night and the day.
Eating lentils at midnight on NYE brings money — they look like little coins. Tradition, not superstition. Allegedly.
Auguri works for everything: Christmas, birthdays, a new house. The universal Italian greeting card.

vocabulary.ex: La Befana viene la notte del 6 gennaio.
vocabulary.exEn: The Befana comes on the night of January 6th.
vocabulary.note: An old lady on a broom who fills stockings with sweets — or coal, if you were naughty. Slightly terrifying, deeply Italian.
